supermarket.note: Buy the frozen plain Chinese steamed buns from the freezer aisle.

general.note: The three amounts are for separate uses, so buy enough to cover all of them.

tools.name: Cleaver
tools.note: The back of a heavy knife works as a substitute for cracking the claws.

tools.name: Food processor
tools.note: A blender can be used in its place.

tools.name: Bowl
tools.note: Three small bowls are needed, one each for the sauce, the cornstarch mixture, and the eggs.

tools.name: Heavy pot
tools.note: Use a large one so there is room for deep-frying the crab.

tools.name: Slotted spoon
tools.note: A spider can be used in its place.

tools.name: Wire rack
tools.note: Set over a baking sheet for draining the crab.

tools.name: Wok
tools.note: Use one with a lid, which the sauce and the crab finish both need.

steps.title: Prep the crabs
points: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes, until they stop moving.
Set the mantou on a plate on the counter to thaw.
Turn each crab on its back, pull off the triangular flap, and lift off the top shell.
Remove the feathery gills and the grey innards, then rinse the crab under cold water.
Cut each body into 4 pieces with the legs attached, and crack each claw once with the back of the cleaver.
Pat every piece completely dry with paper towels.

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics, sauce, and garnishes
points: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, and red chillies with 1 tablespoon of the oil into a coarse paste.
In one small bowl, stir together the stock, ketchup, sweet chilli sauce, sambal oelek, sugar, soy sauce, and salt.
In a second bowl, mix the cornstarch with the cold water.
In the third bowl, beat the eggs.
Slice the scallions, chop the cilantro, and cut the lime into wedges.

steps.title: Fry the crab
points: Pour the 6 cups of oil into the heavy pot.
It should be no more than half full.
Heat over medium-high to 350°F on the thermometer.
Fry the crab in 2 or 3 batches for 2 to 3 minutes each, until the shells turn red.
Lift the pieces out with the slotted spoon and drain them on the rack.
Turn off the heat under the pot and leave it on the back of the stove to cool.

steps.title: Cook the paste in oil
points: Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil in the wok over medium heat.
Add the paste and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens slightly, smells sweet, and the oil starts to separate from it.
Lower the heat if it begins to stick.

steps.title: Simmer the crab in sauce
points: Pour the sauce into the wok and bring it to a simmer.
Add the crab and any juices from the baking sheet, and toss with tongs to coat.
Cover and simmer over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning the pieces once, until the meat inside the thickest part of the body is white and opaque.

steps.title: Fry mantou
points: While the crab simmers, heat the 1/2 cup of oil in the frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the mantou for 3 to 4 minutes, turning them with tongs, until golden on all sides.
Drain on paper towels.

steps.title: Thicken and add eggs
points: Uncover the wok.
Stir the cornstarch mixture again, pour it in, and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Turn the heat to low.
Pour the beaten eggs over the sauce in a thin stream, wait 20 seconds, then stir gently so they set in soft ribbons.
Take the wok off the heat.

steps.title: Plate and serve
points: Spoon the crab and sauce onto a large platter and scatter the scallions and cilantro over the top.
Serve with the lime wedges and the fried mantou for mopping up the sauce.

troubleshooting.problem: The oil spits hard when the crab goes in
troubleshooting.solution: The crab was wet. Pat every piece dry, including inside the cracked claws, and lower the pieces in gently with the slotted spoon.

troubleshooting.problem: The sauce tastes harsh and raw
troubleshooting.solution: The paste was not cooked long enough. Keep it over medium heat until the oil separates and the smell turns sweet before adding the sauce.

troubleshooting.problem: The eggs turn into firm lumps instead of ribbons
troubleshooting.solution: Turn the heat to low before pouring in the eggs, and stir slowly only after they start to set. The sauce was too hot.

troubleshooting.problem: The sauce is thin and runs off the crab
troubleshooting.solution: The cornstarch settled in the bowl. Stir it well just before adding, and let the sauce simmer a full minute afterward.
